title: Photography direction for a community sports club
metaTitle: Photography that shows a club in play
excerpt: Club photographs should show people playing and how a new person starts. Keep trophy pictures off the lead. The frame is part of the argument.
alt: A person gesturing in a meeting, with a laptop showing a colorful layout, a notebook, and a phone on the table. Direction being agreed, which is what a photo brief has to settle.
caption: A person gestures beside a laptop, a notebook, and a phone. Photograph via Unsplash.

faqs.question: What should the lead photograph of a club show?
faqs.answer: Show people in the activity, at a scale where a stranger can name the sport, including a moment of entry if you have one. A lineup with a cup proves a photo day. An empty hall proves the building. Neither proves that a beginner can walk in.

faqs.question: What belongs in a one-page photo brief?
faqs.answer: Subject, crop, light, and a short list of refusals: no trophy as the homepage lead, no stock strangers, no filter that hides the hall. The brief should be usable by a parent with a phone at a real session. Ten honest frames beat a polished picture of a banner.

faqs.question: How should juniors be photographed?
faqs.answer: Follow the governing body's guidance and the club's safeguarding policy, and get consent before a minor's face goes on the site. Prefer frames where the activity is clear and the use is respectful. A tag on a social post is not consent for the homepage.

sources.title: How Long Do Users Stay on Web Pages?

markdown:
Community sports club website photography should show people playing and how a new person starts. Refuse the trophy case as the lead image. The pictures are part of the argument the page is making. A mood dropped under a headline is just decoration with a caption.

A stranger should be able to name the sport and imagine arriving. If the frame cannot do those two things, it is the wrong frame, however sharp it is.

## The picture has to prove the session

Choose photographs from ordinary sessions, taken close enough that the activity is unmistakable and wide enough that a new person can see the shape of the group. A rally, a drill with a coach visible, a junior circle, a crew on the water, a bout in progress. The reader is asking whether this is the hour they would join. Answer with the hour.

Avoid the three pictures clubs default to when they have not decided. A lineup holding a cup. An empty facility at dusk. A handshake in a corridor. Each can be a fine photograph and a bad argument. The lineup proves a photo day. The empty hall proves architecture. The handshake proves manners. None of them proves that a beginner can walk in on Thursday.

Nielsen Norman Group's piece on [how long people stay](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/how-long-do-users-stay-on-web-pages/) puts the first 10 seconds at the center of the decision to stay. On a club homepage those seconds are mostly picture. The headline can say "beginners welcome." The photograph has to agree. If the picture is a closed celebration, the headline is advertising and the picture is the truth the eye believes.

Ballarat Box Sports, a public Hanabi project, is a community sports brand site. The standard to borrow is simple. The brand should look like the sport and the people in it. A photography direction is how you keep that true after the first photoshoot is over, when a volunteer adds pictures from a phone.

## How to start, visible in the frame

At least one lead picture should include the moment of entry. A coach speaking to two new players at the side. Someone borrowing a club bat. A parent at a marked pickup point. Boots lined up because outdoor soles are not allowed on the floor. These frames explain the start without a paragraph.

Caption them as facts. "Coach Leah with first-night players, Tuesday social." The caption does the job a slogan cannot. It names the session the homepage is selling. A caption that says "where champions are made" attaches the wrong story to a useful photograph.

If you only have celebration pictures, go and take the other ones before you redesign. Ten minutes at the start of a session, with permission, will beat a paid hour of people posed against a banner. Ask before you shoot. Tell people where the picture will appear. For anyone under 18, get the consent your sport and your region already require, and keep it. A strong picture you cannot publish is not an asset.

Show variety that matches the offer. If the club says all abilities are welcome, the pictures should include more than the first team. If the club is a serious squad, do not illustrate it with a picnic. The argument and the archive have to match. Mixed pictures that contradict each other are how a site starts to feel like a collage of committees.

## Light, crop, and the set

Direction is a short brief you can hand to a parent with a decent phone. Subject: people playing, plus the start of a session. Crop: activity readable, faces visible when they have consented, no crop so tight the sport disappears. Light: the real hall or the real ground, even if the light is flat. Background: the place as it is, clutter acceptable, advertising hoardings from another event avoided.

Write the refusals in the same brief. No trophy lift as the homepage lead. No drone shot of the roof as the explanation of the club. No stock photograph of strangers in a sport you do not play. No filter that makes the hall look like a nightclub. No logo watermark across the face of the action.

Use one crop ratio for cards and a consistent approach to color. You do not need a stylist. You need the next picture to belong with the last one. A mix of a warm film preset, a harsh flash photo, and a blue-tinted stock image makes even a real club look unfinished. Pick the honest light and stay there.

Black and white is usually a costume for sports. It abstracts the kit color and the court markings that help a stranger recognize the game. Keep color unless you have a strong reason tied to the brand and you can apply it to every picture, including the one taken on a phone in March.

## People, permission, and minors

The argument depends on real members. That creates a duty. Publish adults who have agreed. For juniors, follow the governing body's guidance and the club's own safeguarding policy, and prefer frames where the activity is clear and the use is respectful. A parent who is surprised to find their child on the homepage will not care how well the crop supports your layout.

Do not pull faces from a tagged social post and assume the tag was consent for the website. Ask. Keep a note of who is in the lead images so you can remove one quickly if someone leaves and asks. A direction includes a removal path. It is part of being a club, not an afterthought for the web editor.

Coaches should be identifiable in at least one picture that sits near their name. That ties the about page to the photography. A nameless silhouette next to a biography wastes both. The face is the proof that the biography is a person who will be in the room.

Kit should look like match or training kit the club really wears. A redesign of the website is a bad moment to invent a fashion range you do not own. If the shirts are plain, photograph the plain shirts. Honesty reads as confidence. A borrowed lifestyle wardrobe reads as a different sport.

## Where each picture is allowed to sit

Assign jobs to frames so the trophy shot has a legal home and the homepage stays clear. Homepage lead: people playing, entry visible. Session cards: that session, specifically. About: coaches in the place. Season review: the cup, the squad, the year, late in the site. Sponsors: small, and never over the action.

This assignment is the direction. Without it, every volunteer puts their favorite file in the hero, and the favorite file is often the final. Write the assignment on one page and pin it where images get uploaded. If the site has a portal or a shared folder for brand files, put the brief there so the next editor inherits the rule. Hanabi's client portal is built for that kind of handoff after delivery: files, notes, and the decisions, in one place the club can reopen.

Replace weak images rather than covering them with type. A headline stretched across a confusing crop is a confession that the crop is wrong. Change the crop or change the picture. Type can name the session. It should not have to explain what the pixels failed to show.

A direction also names the file. Date, session, and subject, so "finals-hero-v3" does not become the homepage by accident because it sorts first. The person uploading from a committee laptop should be able to see which file is allowed to lead. Write that permission into the filename and into a one-line note in the folder. When a picture is declined, say why in the same note: trophy lead, no consent, sport unreadable. The next volunteer learns the rule from the refusal, which is faster than a brand workshop they will not attend.

If the club has no recent frames of ordinary play, the right spend is an hour at a real session, not a redesign that crops old celebrations harder. Bring the brief on a phone. Take the entry, the coach, and one moment of the game. You will leave with enough for a homepage, a session card, and a coaches page. That is a complete set. A complete set beats a large archive that argues with itself.

## The phone will crop your favorite frame

Most prospective members will see the picture on a phone, in a tall or square crop, with the headline competing for the same width. Check every lead image at that size before you approve it. A wide celebration photo often becomes a single torso. The sport vanishes. The argument vanishes with it.

The mobile visit is the real visit, and it is where photography direction either holds or falls apart. That pass is covered in [the mobile visit for a community sports club](/blog/the-mobile-visit-for-a-community-sports-club).

If you want to see how a sports brand site carries pictures of the activity, look through [Hanabi's selected work](https://tryhanabi.com/#works). Judge the frames by whether you can tell what people are doing, and how you would start.
